gloss: to accept; to resign oneself to; to content oneself with

definitions.gloss: to accept; to resign oneself to; to submit to
definitions.explanation: To accept an unfavorable situation or outcome without resistance. Implies a passive acceptance of something undesirable, often because one feels powerless to change it or considers it deserved.

definitions.gloss: to content oneself with; to settle for
definitions.explanation: To be satisfied with less than what might be desired or expected. Often used with a critical nuance, suggesting the person should aspire to more.

examples.japanese: {敗北|はいぼく}に{甘|あま}んじるしかなかった。
examples.english: I had no choice but to accept defeat.

examples.japanese: {批判|ひはん}を{受|う}けても、それに{甘|あま}んじて{自分|じぶん}の{信念|しんねん}を{貫|つらぬ}いた。
examples.english: Even when criticized, he accepted it and stuck to his convictions.

examples.japanese: {現状|げんじょう}に{甘|あま}んじてはいけない。
examples.english: You must not settle for the status quo.

examples.japanese: {二位|にい}に{甘|あま}んじるつもりはない。
examples.english: I have no intention of settling for second place.

examples.japanese: {低|ひく}い{給料|きゅうりょう}に{甘|あま}んじていると、いつまでも{生活|せいかつ}は{楽|らく}にならない。
examples.english: If you settle for a low salary, your life will never get easier.

notes:
Derived from {甘|あま}い (sweet, lenient). The verb conveys the idea of passively accepting something, as though yielding to sweetness or leniency. Most commonly appears in the pattern ～に{甘|あま}んじる. The older form {甘|あま}んずる also exists but is rare in modern usage.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {罰|ばつ}に{甘|あま}んじる: to accept punishment
- {現状|げんじょう}に{甘|あま}んじる: to settle for the status quo
- {敗北|はいぼく}に{甘|あま}んじる: to accept defeat
- {批判|ひはん}に{甘|あま}んじる: to accept criticism
- ～に{甘|あま}んじてはいけない: must not settle for ~

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {受|う}け{入|い}れる: to accept — neutral; simply means to accept without the nuance of resignation
- {我慢|がまん}する: to endure, put up with — emphasizes tolerating something unpleasant through willpower
- {諦|あきら}める: to give up — focuses on abandoning hope, while {甘|あま}んじる focuses on accepting a lesser outcome
